ChatGPT said:
FEAT327-ACQ-05 — Animal Companion lifecycle addendum

Adopt a NEW distinction between purchasing the feat and establishing a bond. Spend the bonding attempt at its valid start. Correct “new paid acquisition” so replacement never requires purchasing the same nonrepeatable feat again.

The existing Animal Handling prerequisite, finite bodies, HP conversion, command rules, release hour, beneficial-rest limits and Ranger/EX58 boundaries remain controlling.

I verified the actual PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json: all 21 payload hashes and byte sizes match. The narrow source, guarded-edit, preservation/parity and reference-arithmetic review completed 96 checks with zero failures. I inspected the companion procedures, contracts, relevant shared rules, templates, Ranger source, EX58 work/rest/control provisions and supplied model/report limitations. I did not rerun the reported 110-check suite or execute a companion lifecycle runtime.

Download the complete addendum and evidence package


Controlling addendum
 · 
Exact guarded operations
 · 
Complete corrected Animal Companion procedure

Package: 62,411 bytes; ten payloads plus manifest.
SHA-256: 2e54e75f770b29d242045c892a4db39fefcb3d080c14aeef07747df0dbd41a48

1. Ruling and retained source
Question	Controlling disposition
First purchase	NEW completion: an eligible character commits one actual earned feat opportunity and immediately owns Animal Companion. No animal or completed bonding hour is required to purchase it. The purchase initializes one attempt, not a companion.
Attempt expenditure	NEW completion: spend the attempt atomically when a valid, admitted bonding hour actually begins. An interrupted or abandoned attempt remains spent.
Replacement while already bonded	KEEP one bond and the release requirement: a second bond attempt cannot start while retaining the existing feat bond. Rejecting that proposal neither spends an attempt nor releases the animal.
After release/death	KEEP; make chronology explicit: this owner needs a genuinely beneficial Long Rest completion ordered after the bond-ending event, an available attempt, an eligible living animal and a complete new hour.
Transfer	Correct ambiguous wording: an existing feat owner pays the receiving attempt/hour, not another feat opportunity. A receiver without the feat needs their own legitimate feat acquisition or an independently acquired receiving engine.
Ranger route	KEEP separate: actual Ranger feature acquisition and native costs apply. Animal Companion supplies no Ranger grant, free RP, release permission or substitute chassis.

The exact controlling clauses are preserved in the 
bound source extracts
:

S1/S8: public candidate /feats/10 and acquisition contracts /records/10: Animal Companion’s printed prerequisite, complete procedure and nonrepeatability.
S2–S4: shared rules /rules/0, /rules/5, /rules/9: FS-01, FS-06 and FS-10.
S5–S7: supplements /groups/1 (SUP-02); Ranger /engine/7 and /cards/29.
S9/S11/S12: Companion Training’s actual OR prerequisite; EX58 FL-03 work/rest and TR-02 control/training procedures.

The purchase/start/interruption distinctions below are NEW authoring completions—not claims that the old wording already specified those events. The contradictory “new paid acquisition” phrase is repaired alongside, not by changing, the original feat or its prerequisite tree.

2. Exact replacement wording

Apply these four replacements only within the current Animal Companion operative procedure. The package contains the exact old strings and guarded locations. Its unrelated HP, attack, death, command and mounted-interface text remains unchanged.

ACQ05-PURCHASE-ATTEMPT

Replace the opening span beginning “NEW acquisition:” and ending “One feat bond at a time.” with:

NEW ACQ-05 purchase/bond distinction: acquire Animal Companion once by committing one actual earned unspent feat opportunity while meeting its actual Animal Handling proficiency prerequisite and all other acquisition gates. Record that paid grant and its acquisition snapshot atomically. The animal and bonding hour are not conditions of purchasing the feat. Ownership begins at that commitment, with no companion and one unspent bond attempt under FS-06; it grants neither an animal nor an earlier completed Long Rest. Animal identity, matching template and any actually sourced sense choice belong to each bond record, not a permanently locked feat-purchase choice. The retained nonrepeatability/permanent-choice metadata does not prohibit the replacements expressly allowed here. Canceling a proposed purchase before commitment spends no opportunity. A completed purchase is not refunded or repeated because no animal is available, a bond attempt fails, or a bond later ends. Animal Companion ownership alone can satisfy Companion Training's printed parent alternative, but supplies neither its separate feat opportunity nor a creature on which to use it.

NEW ACQ-05 bond attempt: an owner of this feat with actual Animal Handling proficiency, no current feat bond, no other pending bond attempt, an unspent attempt and any required post-bond-ending Long Rest may select one already real, positive-HP living, willing/tamed, noncorrupted Beast with INT<7 fitting one of the three finite templates. The selected animal must have no incompatible existing bond, including another Animal Companion or Ranger bond. Finding, buying or taming it still needs actual lawful access and its real willing/tamed relationship to this owner; no animal, stocked shop, consent or charm is supplied. Preserve its actual identity, ordinary profile, current/maximum HP, conditions, injuries, native movement, breathing, custody and required template choices. In one ordered start event, recheck admission, reserve this owner and animal for the work, spend the one attempt, and begin the hour. Merely proposing a target or rejecting it before that event does not spend an attempt; it never reverses a previously completed feat purchase. Starting costs no RP, second feat opportunity or universal fee. An attempt cannot begin while an existing feat bond is retained; such a rejected proposal does not release or alter that bond.

Spend one uninterrupted hour of actual bonding work together at touch range. Keep the same owner and animal, actual access, the required proficiency and animal eligibility throughout the work and at completion; the owner must remain able to perform it. This is active work, not beneficial rest, and grants no extra work Watch, assistant shortcut, handover or overlapping incompatible task. Loss of required touch-range access, willing/tamed eligibility, qualifying body state, or the owner's ability to continue, including incapacitation, or voluntary abandonment terminates the attempt. Elapsed time, real losses and the spent attempt persist; no partial hour, resumed fraction or same-epoch retry is awarded. The prospective animal remains in its actual current ordinary state; no feat profile or command entitlement was installed. After a full lawful hour, atomically complete the one bond and apply the existing template/HP conversion to the animal's latest lawful ordinary state, using the owner's then-current governing statistics. No new bond check or success chance is added. Admission alone or an incomplete hour cannot establish a companion.

The initial allowance is one attempt at feat purchase. Each genuinely completed beneficial owner Long Rest thereafter sets the allowance to one, never adds a stored second attempt. Apply FS-06's actual rest limits and one elapsed clock: no reset from Short Rest, debt-only Rest, a repeated rest receipt, a scene, a new target, a new controller, a new day label or level growth. Do not credit active bonding or release work as rest. An invalid claimed completion record is evidence rejection, not an attempt or feat-payment refund: reconcile the real start/interruption/rest history. Missing history cannot be replaced by an assumed unspent allowance. One feat bond at a time.

This preserves the literal willing/tamed alternative. Losing willingness does not automatically prove that an independently qualifying tamed relationship also ceased; the actual admission predicate must be evaluated rather than replaced with a different one.

ACQ05-REPLACEMENT

Replace:

Death/release never creates replacement: after a new completedLR, a new real animal and full hour are required.

With:

NEW ACQ-05 replacement boundary: when an established feat bond ends through release or death, record that actual ending event. Before this owner begins any later feat bond, require a genuinely beneficial owner Long Rest whose completion is ordered after that event, as well as an available attempt, a real eligible living target and the full new hour. A rest completed before the ending event or an unused prior allowance cannot satisfy that replacement gate. A qualifying completion after the event is sufficient; no additional rule requires the whole rest to have started after it. Existing active-work/rest restrictions still apply. Replacement is a use of the already-owned nonrepeatable feat, not a second purchase. NEW explicit rebond interpretation: a previously released living animal may be selected again if it genuinely qualifies; it is a new bond to the same physical individual, not a new or refreshed animal. A dead animal never becomes eligible merely through rest, release, purchase or this procedure.

Consequently, an unsuccessful replacement does not restore the old bond. It already ended before replacement became eligible.

ACQ05-RELEASE

Replace the current sentence beginning “Voluntary release takes one uninterrupted hour…” with:

Voluntary release requires the owner's one uninterrupted hour of actual release work. NEW ACQ-05 release boundary: record its start, but end the bond only on lawful completion; interruption or abandonment grants no partial-hour credit and leaves the existing bond intact unless an independent event already ended it. A fresh release hour may be begun while the bond still exists. Release consumes no bond attempt, feat opportunity or RP. It does not require a second target or borrow the bonding hour's touch-range requirement; actual owner capacity and uninterrupted work remain mandatory. At completion restore the same living animal's saved ordinary profile with the existing positive-current-HP ratio conversion, preserving its current conditions, injuries and actual custody without healing or refilling it. End the outgoing bond's control entitlement and unexecuted commands; preserve all already-spent body/actor allowances. No automatic transfer of custody or command occurs. Record this end for the post-ending Long-Rest gate.

The old text specified an uninterrupted release hour, not a second touch-range bonding ritual. This completion does not add that extra range restriction. It also does not let release work count simultaneously as beneficial rest.

ACQ05-TRANSFER

Replace:

A creature cannot have this and a Ranger bond simultaneously; transferring requires actual release and new paid acquisition, not additive statistics.

With:

A creature cannot simultaneously have this and a Ranger bond, or two owners' Animal Companion bonds. NEW ACQ-05 correction of 'new paid acquisition': a transfer requires the outgoing bond to end through its actual lawful release/death/termination procedure, real lawful access/custody for the receiver, and the receiver's independently authorized new bond. An existing Animal Companion feat owner does not buy that nonrepeatable feat again; they spend their own available attempt and full hour and satisfy their own post-ending Long-Rest gate, if any. The sender's rest, feat ownership or spent attempt neither transfers nor resets the receiver's history. A receiver without this feat must first acquire it through their own actual eligible unspent opportunity, or use an independently acquired receiving engine; receiving the animal grants no feat or class feature. An actual Ranger Beast Companion route retains its own acquired Warder/class-level/selection gates, eligible-beast limits, 4 RP, one-hour touch procedure, once-per-beneficial-owner-Long-Rest allowance and native profile/lifecycle. This feat's no-RP route, release hour and attempt rules do not waive or redefine that class engine. A Ranger bond cannot be ended by invoking another engine's feat-release permission. No universal transfer payment, new animal, healing, additive chassis, second controller, extra phase or refunded body/resource budget is granted.

The actual Ranger comparison is ranger.hero.warder.beast-companion, ranger.json /cards/29: an acquired Warder selection at Ranger 16, not an automatic grant to every Ranger. Engine /engine/7 retains the eligible Beast restrictions, including CR no greater than Ranger class level. Its original source and current status remain unchanged.

This does not prohibit independently lawful ordinary animal handling or Companion Training’s existing lawful-control scope. Those permissions simply do not grant the Animal Companion chassis.

3. Deterministic lifecycle

The state distinction is:

Paid feat ownership → available attempt → admitted, spent attempt → completed bond or terminal unsuccessful attempt.

A bond ending introduces a separate post-ending beneficial-rest requirement. Having an unused attempt does not bypass that requirement.

A concrete conditional sequence illustrates the complete ordering:

Event	Result
Last beneficial LR completes at hour 0. At hour 1, a proficient Warrior 4 pays its real level-4 opportunity. No animal is present.	Feat owned; no bond; one attempt.
A valid attempt starts at hour 2. Contact is lost at 2:20.	Attempt spent; hour terminated; ordinary animal remains ordinary. Feat payment persists.
Another attempt is proposed at hour 3.	Rejected: no available attempt.
A genuinely supported eight-hour Rest from 16–24 completes a new beneficial LR.	One attempt restored. The failed attempt remains in history.
A new full hour from 24–25 succeeds. The actual Small ground animal is then at ordinary 5/10 HP.	One bond; current/max HP becomes 4/9 at owner level 4. No full-health reset.
A later beneficial LR completes at 48 while the bond exists.	Attempt becomes one, but a second bond still cannot start.
Release work from 49–50 completes.	Bond ends. The same animal returns to ordinary 4/10 under the retained ratio conversion.
Replacement is proposed immediately at 50, using the unused attempt.	Rejected: the owner still needs a beneficial LR completion after the bond ended.
The next actual eligible completion occurs at 72; a new attempt runs 72–73.	No second feat purchase. Success establishes the new bond; interruption leaves the owner unbonded and the attempt spent.

These are authored conditional premises, not campaign receipts. Actual rest support, animal identity, access and time must be represented in the later candidate examples.

Transfer does not impose the sender’s rest gate on a different receiver. A receiving feat owner uses their own allowance and their own previous-bond-ending history. A first-time receiver can use their legitimate initial allowance after buying the feat; they do not inherit the sender’s feat, rest or controller record.

4. Exact affected derived locations

The package supplies seven guarded replacements across five existing files.

File	Current locations to change
DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/data/public/feat_candidates/exact_01/candidate.json	/feats/10/operationalRules; /feats/10/payloadOperational
DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/data/director/feat_candidates/exact_01/candidate.json	/records/161/operationalRules; /records/161/payloadOperational
docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/FEAT_EXACT_01_ACQUISITION_CONTRACTS.json	/records/10/completeOperativeProcedure
DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/feats/exact-candidate-01/GENERAL_COMBAT.md	Animal Companion’s current operative procedure
DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/feats/exact-candidate-01/source-audit/GENERAL_COMBAT.md	GC-04’s current candidate procedure, with the packaged explicit controlling-addendum note

Guard each JSON record by id == "animal_companion", not its array position alone.

Preserve unchanged: sourceObject, originalObject, prerequisite trees, repeats metadata, original335Registry, all sourceDirection fields, the audit’s preserved submitted procedure/examples and original source decision, all unrelated feats, shared rules, supplements, Ranger/class sources, EX58 and every approval/selection flag.

In particular, the old sourceDirection.completeAuthoringProcedure remains historical. It must not overwrite the corrected current procedure through an older renderer. Append the addendum and measured descendant bindings without replacing original source hashes.

Necessary model/evidence adjustment

The supplied CompanionAcquisition.acquire_companion_from_completed_history currently calls pay.commit after validating the completed hour. Preserve that model and report as their historical revision, but do not use that staging as the new purchase rule.

A new derived model or read-only history adapter must distinguish:

earlier paid acquisition → admitted attempt-start expenditure → completion/interruption.

Its existing four successful HP endpoints remain compatible: at owner level 4, the submitted ordinary body states produce 4, 1, 3 and 6 current HP, each with maximum 9. Growth to owner level 8 changes maximum to 13, not current HP or the spent allowance.

Rejected completion evidence no longer implies that an independently proved prior feat purchase never occurred. Nor does it imply the attempt was refunded.

5. Finite acceptance expectations

The full premises and outcomes are in 
ACQ05_ACCEPTANCE_EXPECTATIONS.json
. These twenty groups are authored expectations, not lifecycle tests executed in this review.

Case	Required outcome
T01 — Purchase without animal	Valid payment establishes ownership and one attempt, with no companion.
T02 — Invalid/duplicate purchase	No new grant, payment or reinitialization. A completed legitimate purchase is not refunded by later cancellation.
T03 — First valid hour	Spend at start; install no chassis before lawful completion; no additional opportunity, RP or roll.
T04 — Four body endpoints	Preserve the four numerical HP results and later nonhealing growth described above.
T05 — Invalid preflight	Reject before start without spending an attempt; retain any already-paid feat. Missing evidence does not prove no earlier attempt occurred.
T06 — Interrupted attempt	Contact/access/eligibility loss, incapacitation, abandonment or death terminates the attempt without partial credit or refund.
T07 — Same-epoch retry	Changing scene, target, date or controller label cannot supply another attempt.
T08 — Genuine LR recovery	Set allowance to one after an actual new beneficial owner LR; never bank two.
T09 — False recovery	Short Rest, debt-only Rest, duplicate receipt, an ineligible LR or overlapping active work supplies no reset.
T10 — Existing bond retained	Reject replacement start; retain the old bond and do not spend an attempt through the rejected proposal.
T11 — Interrupted release	Retain the bond unless another event ended it. A later release requires a fresh full hour, with no attempt charge.
T12 — Completed release	Restore the same ordinary body proportionally, preserve condition/custody, and enforce the subsequent beneficial-rest requirement.
T13 — Animal/owner death	Retain the distinct existing death outcomes; no revival, replacement animal or allowance reset.
T14 — Failed replacement	Keep the old bond ended and the new attempt spent. A lawful rebond preserves the actual individual rather than creating a refreshed body.
T15 — Receiving existing feat owner	Receiver spends their own attempt/hour and satisfies their own applicable rest gate; no second feat purchase.
T16 — Receiving nonowner/Ranger	No free feat from custody. A real first feat purchase or independently acquired Ranger route supplies only its own permissions and costs.
T17 — Incompatible outgoing bond	No incoming bond until the outgoing engine genuinely ends. Feat release supplies no Ranger-release authority.
T18 — Physical/control conservation	Preserve latest HP, injuries, identity, custody and spent budgets; no extra mounted/companion phase or additive chassis.
T19 — Invalid completion record	Reject the completion without erasing an actual earlier payment or spent start.
T20 — Child prerequisite/preservation	Owned Animal Companion can satisfy Companion Training’s parent alternative without a current animal; its separate opportunity and actual use predicates remain required. Preserve all unrelated fields and flags.
Final disposition

These three acquisition/attempt/transfer questions are settled for source authoring. Apply the named edits, preserve the original revisions, verify current procedure parity and record the finite acceptance outcomes. That fulfillment needs no new generic source conference.

The later complete feat exact review remains separate. This addendum does not approve all 335 acquisitions, the unfinished candidate, class content, gameplay implementation, human balance or whole-game flow. ACQ-03/04 and the completed scopes remain carried forward.

The CRPG direction and unchanged twelve-character, parallel-activity, host-permission expedition remain controlling. Delivery remains actual final joint whole-game flow agreement → already-authorized commit/push → verified remote commit → careful cosmology review and preservation-based cleanup in their agreed phases.
